headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This legislation shifts the financial burden of new grid infrastructure from residential ratepayers to large energy consumers, primarily data centers, ensuring they bear the costs associated with their significant energy demands.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Consumer advocates, residential ratepayers, environmental groups.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Abigail Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393, a key energy measure designed to shift more costs onto data centers and large manufacturers to save residential electricity customers money. Critics, including the bill's sponsor, believe the governor's proposed amendments could weaken the bill's intended impact.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that data centers report their water consumption, providing transparency and data for future water resource management and policy decisions.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local governments, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (due to increased reporting burden).
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, mandates that local water authorities report data center water usage, making the numbers publicly available on the Department of Environmental Quality's website. This aims to provide transparency and address concerns about the industry's water consumption, despite data centers arguing their usage is a small percentage of total state withdrawals.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise
short_summary: This legislation addresses the placement of new data centers and establishes limits on noise pollution to mitigate impacts on surrounding communities.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near proposed data center sites, environmental advocates, Delegate Josh Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: New siting requirements for large data centers in Virginia
news_summary: HB 153 introduces new siting requirements for large data centers, mandating impact assessments on sound profiles for homes and schools within 500 feet, as well as potential effects on agriculture, parks, and historical sites before rezoning approval. This legislation is seen as a foundation for stronger future regulations on data center placement and community impact.
